Echo State Networks (ESNs) are a type of recurrent neural network used for processing time series data. They consist of a large, fixed-size, randomly connected hidden layer called the "reservoir," which processes the input data. The weights of the reservoir are typically fixed and not trained, making the training process simpler. Only the output weights are adjusted to fit the desired output. Reservoir computing is a framework that includes ESNs and other similar architectures, which are used for tasks like signal processing and time series prediction.
